quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud in a formal, careful voice.
quests.hint: Formal speech keeps full forms and clear endings: 'would like to', not 'wanna'; every final consonant is audible.
quests.explanation: Formal pronunciation slows down slightly, keeps weak forms clear, and avoids heavy reductions. The stress falls on enQUIRE, availaBILity, CONference and JUNE.
quests.textToSpeak: I would like to enquire about the availability of the conference room in June.
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪ wʊd ˈlaɪk tuː ɪnˈkwaɪər əˈbaʊt ði əˌveɪləˈbɪləti əv ðə ˈkɒnfərəns ˈruːm ɪn ˈdʒuːn].
commonMistakes: Dropping the final [t] or [d] of words

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud in a relaxed, casual voice.
quests.hint: Informal speech uses reductions: 'have you got a' runs together, 'wanted to' becomes 'wantid-ta', and 'ask you' becomes 'ask-ya'.
quests.explanation: Casual pronunciation squeezes function words and links them. Keep the content words 'sec', 'ask' and 'quick' clear.
quests.textToSpeak: Hey, have you got a sec? I wanted to ask you something quick.
quests.phoneticHint: [heɪ əv jə ˈgɒt ə ˈsek] | [aɪ ˈwɒntɪd tə ˈæsk jə ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈkwɪk].

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a polite reply to an invitation.
quests.hint: Semi-formal keeps contractions but clear stress: 'won't', 'able', 'attend', 'appreciate', 'invitation'.
quests.explanation: This register sits between the two: use natural rhythm and contractions, but finish words fully and keep the stressed syllables clear.
quests.textToSpeak: Unfortunately, I won't be able to attend, but I really appreciate the invitation.
quests.phoneticHint: [ʌnˈfɔːrtʃənətli aɪ ˈwoʊnt bi ˈeɪbəl tu əˈtend bət aɪ ˈrɪəli əˈpriːʃieɪt ði ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən].
commonMistakes: Saying 'won't' as 'wont' with a weak vowel

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a clinical update.
quests.hint: 'diagnosis' stresses NO, 'prescription' stresses SCRIP, and 'inflammation' stresses MAY.
quests.explanation: Latin-based medical words follow the -tion and -sis stress rules: stress on the syllable before the ending. Keep the first syllable weak.
quests.textToSpeak: The specialist confirmed the diagnosis and wrote a prescription for the inflammation.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a patient at an appointment.
quests.hint: 'symptoms' has an [mpt] cluster, 'persistent' stresses SIS, and 'breath' ends in [θ].
quests.explanation: In 'symptoms', the [p] is often lightly pronounced: [ˈsɪmptəmz]. 'breath' [breθ] differs from 'breathe' [briːð] in vowel and final sound.
quests.textToSpeak: My symptoms include a persistent cough, a mild fever and shortness of breath.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a hospital briefing.
quests.hint: 'cardiologist' stresses OL, 'anaesthetist' stresses NAES, and 'procedure' stresses CEE.
quests.explanation: -ologist words stress the syllable 'ol'. 'ECG' is a letter sequence stressed on the last letter. 'procedure' has a [dʒ] sound in its last syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: The cardiologist recommended an ECG, and the anaesthetist explained the procedure.

quests.instruction: Read it slowly first, then at natural speed (legal vocabulary: -ity, -tion).
quests.hint: 'agreement' stresses GREE, 'liability' stresses BIL, and 'jurisdiction' stresses DIC.
quests.explanation: Long legal words follow the suffix rules you know: -ity and -tion pull stress to the syllable before the ending. 'clause' ends with [z].
quests.textToSpeak: The agreement includes a clause on liability and a jurisdiction section.
commonMistakes: Saying 'jurisdiction' with four beats of equal weight

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a courtroom report.
quests.hint: 'plaintiff' is PLAIN-tiff, 'lawyer' is LOY-er, 'defendant' is de-FEN-dant, and 'signature' is SIG-na-chur.
quests.explanation: 'lawyer' has [ɔɪ] in the first syllable. 'plaintiff' has [eɪ] and ends with a weak [ɪf]. 'signature' has [tʃ] in the last syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: The plaintiff's lawyer questioned the defendant about the signature.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a to-do list.
quests.hint: 'negotiate' has [ʃ] and stress on GO, 'warranty' stresses WAR, and 'paperwork' stresses PA.
quests.explanation: In 'negotiate', the [ʃ] comes from the letters 'ti'. 'warranty' is [ˈwɔːrənti] with a rounded first vowel. 'paperwork' stresses the first part.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's negotiate the terms, review the warranty, and file the paperwork before Friday.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a tech explanation.
quests.hint: 'algorithm' stresses AL and ends in a weak [ðəm]; 'authentication' stresses KAY; 'database' stresses DAY.
quests.explanation: 'algorithm' has a [ð] in the middle, not [θ]. 'authentication' starts with [ɔː] and follows the -tion stress pattern.
quests.textToSpeak: The algorithm needs authentication before it can access the database.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a home-network complaint.
quests.hint: 'router' rhymes with 'outer' or 'tooter'; 'bandwidth' ends in [dθ]; 'buffering' stresses BUF.
quests.explanation: 'bandwidth' combines [ndw] and [dθ]; take time on the ending. 'buffering' is [ˈbʌfərɪŋ].
quests.textToSpeak: Our router has limited bandwidth, so the video keeps buffering.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as tech-support advice.
quests.hint: 'cache' sounds like 'cash', 'software' stresses SOFT, and 'encryption' stresses CRIP.
quests.explanation: 'cache' is [kæʃ], one syllable. 'encryption' follows the -tion rule: stress on the syllable before -tion.
quests.textToSpeak: Clear the cache, update the software, and check that encryption is turned on.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a financial summary.
quests.hint: 'revenue' stresses REV, 'liabilities' stresses BIL, and 'depreciation' stresses AY.
quests.explanation: 'revenue' has three syllables with stress on the first. 'depreciation' is a five-syllable -tion word: stress on the syllable before -tion.
quests.textToSpeak: The company's revenue rose, but its liabilities and depreciation also increased.
commonMistakes: Making 'liabilities' stressed equally on all syllables

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a homebuyer.
quests.hint: 'mortgage' has a silent t; 'interest' is IN-trest in two or three syllables.
quests.explanation: 'mortgage' is [ˈmɔːrgɪdʒ]. 'interest' is often said as [ˈɪntrəst] or [ˈɪntərəst]; either is acceptable, but keep stress on the first syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: We're applying for a mortgage, and the interest rate is lower than last year.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an investment comment.
quests.hint: 'equity' stresses EK, 'assets' stresses AS, and 'appreciate' stresses PREE and ends in [eɪt].
quests.explanation: 'equity' has [kw]. 'appreciate' as a verb ends with a full [eɪt]; the noun 'appreciation' has -tion.
quests.textToSpeak: The investor bought equity in the startup, hoping the assets will appreciate.
commonMistakes: Saying 'appreciate' with a weak ending, as 'appreciut'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a travel agent.
quests.hint: 'itinerary' stresses TIN, 'complimentary' stresses MEN, and 'transfer' as a noun stresses TRANS.
quests.explanation: 'complimentary' has five syllables with stress on the third. 'itinerary' begins with [aɪ] and stresses the second syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: Your itinerary includes complimentary breakfast and a private transfer.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a hotel recommendation.
quests.hint: 'concierge' stresses AIRZH, 'vegetarian' stresses TAIR, and 'theatre' stresses THEE.
quests.explanation: 'concierge' is French: [ˌkɒnsiˈeəʒ] with a final [ʒ]. 'vegetarian' has [dʒ] in the first syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: The concierge can recommend a vegetarian restaurant near the theatre.
commonMistakes: Saying 'theatre' with the stress on the second syllable

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a restaurant customer.
quests.hint: 'allergic' stresses LER and has [dʒ]; 'gluten' stresses GLOO; 'wheat' begins with [w].
quests.explanation: 'allergic' has a [dʒ] from 'g' before 'i'. 'gluten' is [ˈgluːtən], with stress on the first syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm allergic to gluten, so could you check whether the sauce contains wheat?

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an engineering report.
quests.hint: 'aluminium' has five syllables (al-yu-MIN-ee-um) in British English, and 'calibrated' stresses KAL.
quests.explanation: American English says 'aluminum' with four syllables. Either way, don't drop the [j] sound near the start. 'tolerance' is [ˈtɒlərəns].
quests.textToSpeak: The aluminium frame was tested for tolerance and calibrated before assembly.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a technical description.
quests.hint: 'schematic' begins with [sk], 'sequence' stresses SEE, and 'specifications' stresses KAY.
quests.explanation: 'sch' in 'schematic' is [sk], as in 'school'. 'specifications' is a five-syllable -tion word with stress just before the ending.
quests.textToSpeak: The schematic shows the sequence of operations and the specifications for each part.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a failure report.
quests.hint: 'hydraulic' stresses DRAW and has [ɔː]; 'valve' ends in [lv]; 'pressure' ends in [ʃər].
quests.explanation: 'hydraulic' begins with [haɪ] and the stress falls on the second syllable. 'valve' ends in a [lv] cluster: keep the [l] before the [v].
quests.textToSpeak: The hydraulic system failed because a valve stuck under pressure.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud at a fast, natural pace.
quests.hint: Speed comes from reduced small words; clarity comes from stressed content: MEANing, TELL, BUSy, CHANCE, SIT, GO, EVeryTHING, PROPerly.
quests.explanation: At speed, don't rush the content words. Squeeze 'I've been', 'it's been', 'to' and 'through' quickly, and keep the strong words clear.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been meaning to tell you, but it's been so busy that I haven't had a chance to sit down and go through everything properly.
quests.phoneticHint: [aɪv bɪn ˈmiːnɪŋ tə ˈtel ju bət ɪts bɪn soʊ ˈbɪzi ðət aɪ ˈhævənt hæd ə ˈtʃæns tə ˈsɪt ˈdaʊn ən ˈgoʊ θruː ˈevriθɪŋ ˈprɒpərli].
commonMistakes: Saying every word at the same speed and strength
Swallowing the ends of content words

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a manager planning.
quests.hint: Two chunks: the condition (PROPosal, apPROVED, WEDnesday) and the plan (eNOUGH TIME, BRIEF, START, WORK).
quests.explanation: Chunking makes fast speech easy to follow: say the 'if' clause quickly and finish it with a small rise, then say the main clause with a fall.
quests.textToSpeak: If we can get the proposal approved by Wednesday, we'll have enough time to brief the team and start the work next week.
quests.phoneticHint: [ɪf wi kən ˈget ðə prəˈpoʊzəl əˈpruːvd baɪ ˈwenzdeɪ] | [wil hæv ɪˈnʌf ˈtaɪm tə ˈbriːf ðə ˈtiːm ənd ˈstɑːrt ðə ˈwɜːrk ˈnekst ˈwiːk].
commonMistakes: Failing to pause between the two clauses

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a candid opinion.
quests.hint: 'overcomplicating' stresses COM, 'ownership' stresses OWN, and 'simple plan' peaks on SIM and PLAN.
quests.explanation: The long word 'overcomplicating' needs a strong [ɒ] in COM and quick, weak syllables around it. The final phrase 'someone to take ownership' links smoothly.
quests.textToSpeak: Honestly, I think we're overcomplicating this; all we really need is a simple plan and someone to take ownership.
quests.targetPhoneme: fast intelligible speech with long words
quests.phoneticHint: [ˈɒnɪstli aɪ ˈθɪŋk wɪr ˌoʊvərˈkɒmplɪkeɪtɪŋ ðɪs ˈɔːl wi ˈrɪəli ˈniːd ɪz ə ˈsɪmpəl ˈplæn ənd ˈsʌmwʌn tə ˈteɪk ˈoʊnərʃɪp].
commonMistakes: Saying 'ownership' as 'own-er-ship' with three equal beats

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a policy comment.
quests.hint: 'demographic' stresses GRAF, 'infrastructure' stresses IN, and 'data' stresses DAY.
quests.explanation: 'demographic' follows the -ic rule; 'infrastructure' has a [str] cluster in the middle and a [tʃ] at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: According to the latest data, the demographic shift will put pressure on infrastructure.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a research finding.
quests.hint: 'statistically' stresses TIS, 'significant' stresses NIF, and 'relatively' stresses REL.
quests.explanation: 'statistically' is a five-syllable word with the stress on the third; the -ly ending is quick. 'sample' [ˈsæmpəl] has an [mp] cluster.
quests.textToSpeak: The results are statistically significant, but the sample size was relatively small.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a strategy statement.
quests.hint: 'sustainable' stresses TAIN, 'investment' stresses VEST, and 'cooperation' stresses PER.
quests.explanation: 'sustainable' begins with a weak [sə]. 'cooperation' is a five-syllable -tion word, and 'stakeholders' stresses the first part.
quests.textToSpeak: A sustainable strategy requires long-term investment and cooperation between stakeholders.

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as an administrative update.
quests.hint: Mixed: 'unfortunately' (FOR), 'specialist' (SPESH), 'diagnosis' (NO), 'department' (PART), 'wrong' with a silent w, and 'February'.
quests.explanation: Apply the rules together: stress the syllable before -ist and -sis, keep -ment weak, leave the w silent in 'wrong', and pronounce the r in the middle of 'February'.
quests.textToSpeak: Unfortunately, the specialist's diagnosis was delayed because the paperwork went to the wrong department in February.
quests.targetPhoneme: review: professional vocabulary and silent letters
quests.phoneticHint: [ʌnˈfɔːrtʃənətli ðə ˈspeʃəlɪsts ˌdaɪəgˈnoʊsɪs wəz dɪˈleɪd bɪˈkɒz ðə ˈpeɪpərwɜːrk ˈwent tə ðə ˈrɒŋ dɪˈpɑːrtmənt ɪn ˈfebruːeri].
commonMistakes: Leaving out the [r] in the middle of 'February'

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a contract review.
quests.hint: 'sixth' ends in [ksθ], 'liability' stresses BIL, and 'wording' has [ɜːr].
quests.explanation: Take a breath before 'sixth' and give the [θ] full time. In 'wording', the [ɜːr] is the same vowel as in 'work'.
quests.textToSpeak: The sixth clause covers liability; check the wording carefully before you sign.
quests.phoneticHint: [ðə ˈsɪksθ ˈklɔːz ˈkʌvərz ˌlaɪəˈbɪləti ˈtʃek ðə ˈwɜːrdɪŋ ˈkeərfəli bɪˈfɔːr ju ˈsaɪn].
commonMistakes: Making 'liability' four syllables with equal stress

quests.instruction: Read the sentence aloud as a technical summary.
quests.hint: 'calibrated' stresses KAL, 'aluminium' stresses MIN, 'remarkably' stresses MARK, and 'eighth' ends in [tθ].
quests.explanation: Four rules in one sentence: -ate verbs stress the syllable two before the ending, -ably stresses the syllable before it, and 'eighth' has a difficult ending.
quests.textToSpeak: Our engineers calibrated the aluminium sensors, and the results stayed remarkably consistent through the eighth trial.
quests.phoneticHint: [aʊər ˌendʒɪˈnɪrz ˈkælɪbreɪtɪd ði ˌæljəˈmɪniəm ˈsensərz ənd ðə rɪˈzʌlts ˈsteɪd rɪˈmɑːrkəbli kənˈsɪstənt θruː ði ˈeɪtθ ˈtraɪəl].
